# sad

> Rust CLI for a deterministic documentation gate: comments and doc strings
> outside four structural channels are findings, because prose is evidence
> the code failed to express itself.

sad gates in-code prose. No network, no models, no randomness: same input
tree plus the same repo ledgers, same findings. The premise is that code
should be self-explanatory — the fix for a finding is a refactor into
simpler, more expressive code, not more words.

## Channels

Prose is legitimate in exactly four structurally checkable places:

- **File header** — a top-of-file block containing `Purpose`,
  `Responsibilities`, and `Rationale` (gated by `require_header`).
- **Doc channel** — doc comments and docstrings; the summary lead (text up
  to the first blank line) is capped at `doc_summary_cap` sentences,
  everything after the first blank line is uncapped.
- **Traceability markers** — `marker_prefix` + an ID matching
  `marker_pattern` that resolves against `.beads/issues.jsonl` or
  `openspec/specs/`.
- **Rationale** — a leading `SAFETY:`, `INVARIANT:`, `SECURITY:`, or
  `WHY:` tag with a non-empty body, counted in `stats.comments_rationale`.

Licence/SPDX headers and licence lines beside them, `@generated` regions,
`exclude` globs, Python file metadata (a shebang on source line 1, a PEP
263 coding cookie on lines 1–2), and every suppression directive (`# noqa`,
`# type: ignore`, `// @ts-ignore`, `// @ts-expect-error`,
`// eslint-disable-*`, `sad:ignore <check-id> <reason>`) are
exempt-but-counted: the envelope reports header/doc counts, markers
resolved, rationale count, exemptions, and suppression debt.

## Checks

- `comment_outside_channel` — prose attributed to no channel
- `commented_out_code` — prose block whose normalised body is code-shaped
- `doc_summary_cap_exceeded` — doc summary lead over the cap
- `unresolvable_marker` — marker-prefixed ID that resolves to nothing
- `missing_header` — first block lacks a required header keyword
- `suppression_cap_exceeded` — file over `suppression_cap` suppressions

Each finding carries `severity`. Errors block: narration, apology, todo,
`commented_out_code`, and the structural findings. Warnings report: banner,
unclassified, and the doc cap.

## Commands

- `sad check` — gate the default attribution scope; exits 0 on pass, 1
  when blocking findings exist
- `sad check --all` — analyze every non-excluded file
- `sad check --adopt` — write and commit `sad-baseline.json` (shrink-only
  baseline of grandfathered finding IDs, then evaluate against it)
- `sad version` — tool identity as a genesis suite envelope
- `sad doctor [--fix]` — structured diagnostics for the cwd: `sad.toml`
  validity, the `sad-check` managed block in `.lefthook.yml` (warns with a
  `sad hooks install` remediation; `--fix` wires it), and
  `sad-baseline.json` integrity; ok:false only on failed checks
- `sad feedback <kind> [--title <t>] [--dry-run] [--from-last-error]` —
  file an issue (bug|feature|question|chore) against `charly-vibes/sad`
  via `gh`; reporting-only, never affects check results
- `sad completions <shell>` — print shell completions (bash, zsh, fish,
  powershell, elvish); raw stdout, not an envelope

Global flags: `--json` (raw envelope). Flags accepted by `check`: `--all`,
`--adopt`, `--strict`, `--config <path>` (default: `./sad.toml`, else
built-in defaults).

## Install

```bash
# macOS
brew install charly-vibes/charly/sad

# Windows
scoop bucket add charly https://github.com/charly-vibes/scoop-charly
scoop install sad

# From source
cargo install --path sad --locked
```
